summary: Umpqua NF lookout in Lane County, Oregon: a pole L-4 tower built in 1933 and later listed as gone; sources give its height as 30, 40 or 43 feet.

facts.design: Round fir pole tower with an L-4 model 1931 cab (Rex's page); the register and firelookout.com call it a 30-foot pole L-4 tower
facts.status_note: The register and firelookout.com both list the tower as gone; neither gives a removal date

staffing.status: lookout at the post during a July 1938 inspection, per a district ranger's letter quoted on Rex's page; no staffing start or end dates in these sources

events.note: Built in 1933 per the register and firelookout.com; Rex's page describes the new tower as 43 feet with an L-4 model 1931 cab, and a September 1933 item said the CCC would build a 14x14 lookout

District Ranger Brown inspected the tower and house on July 20, 1938; the letter says the sway made the fire finder impossible to keep level and recommends replacing the cable braces with pole braces

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 30 feet. A July 1938 inspection letter quoted on Rex's page says 40 feet. Rex's 1933 description says 43 feet, which matches the brief's 13.1 m. The story reports all three and does not choose one; height_m keeps the 43-foot figure because that is the only source describing the tower as built.

notes_for_editor: Brief record is accurate on status (gone), county, and elevation (1539 m). The brief's height_m 13.1 matches Rex's 43-foot figure, but the register and firelookout.com say 30 feet and the 1938 letter says 40 feet; check which figure the editor wants on the record. No source gives a removal date or describes the site today; the register's 2007 site photo (courtesy of Ron Kemnow) was not viewed. The Rex page's remains heading has no text under it. Search results also mention a Swastika Mountain lookout 2 1/4 miles northwest of Holland Point, a different structure that was not used.
